newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS - Belgian GBL ups stake in French Suez-Lyonnaise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Belgian GBL ups stake in French Suez-Lyonnaise.

text.p: Belgium's Electrafina, an investment vehicle in holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, said on Tuesday it had upped its stake to nine percent in the soon-to-be-merged French group Suez/Lyonnaise.
Belgian financier Albert Frere, chairman of Electrafina and GBL, told shareholders Electrafina so far had invested about 35 billion francs in the Suez-Lyonnaise group.
"It is clear that we have confidence in the Suez/Lyonnaise management and its strategy," he said.
The merger between Compagnie de Suez and French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux is to be completed later this year.
The merged French group is seeking to become a world leader in collective services, notable energy, water and waste management.
A source close to Electrafina told Reuters the company had bought about three percent of Lyonnaise shares on the Paris bourse in order to boost its stake in the merged group to nine percent.

Asked what his further plans were with the stake, Frere gave no indications, saying: "It is too soon to speculate about the future of this asset. Like all our assets it could in time generate a capital gain for us, which is our aim."

Frere also indicated that he had no plans to unwind the intricate web of holding companies through which he controls choice assets in the energy, banking, media and insurance sectors. A merger of Electrafina and its parent GBL is not in the cards, he said.
"We have considered a merger of GBL and Electrafina, but the issue is not the order of the day right now," Frere said in reply to a question at the annual meeting of Electrafina shareholders.

He said the GBL/Electrafina group only had a limited number of strategic assets and a merger would not improve clarity or decision-making. A merger would however reduce the group's choice of partners and financing.
At the Electrafina meeting Frere, aged 71, also indicated for the first time that he is thinking about his succession.
"One day I too will have to think about retiring," he said in an answer to a question at the annual shareholders' meeting.
"The young colleagues seated with me at the table will assure a good succession," he said.

Frere was flanked by Electrafina chief executive officer Thiery de Rudder and by Didier Bellens, who is part of the management of Luxembourg broadcaster Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion SA (CLT), controlled by Electrafina's Audiofina. Bellens also plays a leading role in GBL.
